patches.old:
check_min_reqs() {
    local hasMinimum=false
    if machine_has "curl"; then
        hasMinimum=true
    elif machine_has "wget"; then
        hasMinimum=true
    fi

    if [ "$hasMinimum" = "false" ]; then
        say_err "curl (recommended) or wget are required to download dotnet. Install missing prerequisite to proceed."
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

download() {
    eval $invocation

    local remote_path="$1"
    local out_path="${2:-}"

    if [[ "$remote_path" != "http"* ]]; then
        cp "$remote_path" "$out_path"
        return $?
    fi

    local failed=false
    local attempts=0
    while [ $attempts -lt 3 ]; do
        attempts=$((attempts+1))
        failed=false
        if machine_has "curl"; then
            downloadcurl "$remote_path" "$out_path" || failed=true
        elif machine_has "wget"; then
            downloadwget "$remote_path" "$out_path" || failed=true
        else
            say_err "Missing dependency: neither curl nor wget was found."
            exit 1
        fi

        if [ "$failed" = false ] || [ $attempts -ge 3 ] || { [ -n "${http_code-}" ] && [ "${http_code}" = "404" ]; }; then
            break
        fi

        say "Download attempt #$attempts has failed: ${http_code-} ${download_error_msg-}"
        say "Attempt #$((attempts+1)) will start in $((attempts*10)) seconds."
        sleep $((attempts*10))
    done

    if [ "$failed" = true ]; then
        say_verbose "Download failed: $remote_path"
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

patches.old:
get_specific_product_version() {
    # If we find a 'productVersion.txt' at the root of any folder, we'll use its contents
    # to resolve the version of what's in the folder, superseding the specified version.
    # if 'productVersion.txt' is missing but download link is already available, product version will be taken from download link
    eval $invocation

    local azure_feed="$1"
    local specific_version="${2//[$'\t\r\n']}"
    local package_download_link=""
    if [ $# -gt 2  ]; then
        local package_download_link="$3"
    fi
    local specific_product_version=null

    # Try to get the version number, using the productVersion.txt file located next to the installer file.
    local download_links=($(get_specific_product_version_url "$azure_feed" "$specific_version" true "$package_download_link")
        $(get_specific_product_version_url "$azure_feed" "$specific_version" false "$package_download_link"))

    for download_link in "${download_links[@]}"
    do
        say_verbose "Checking for the existence of $download_link"

        if machine_has "curl"
        then
            if ! specific_product_version=$(curl -sL --fail "${download_link}${feed_credential}" 2>&1); then
                continue
            else
                echo "${specific_product_version//[$'\t\r\n']}"
                return 0
            fi

        elif machine_has "wget"
        then
            specific_product_version=$(wget -qO- "${download_link}${feed_credential}" 2>&1)
            if [ $? = 0 ]; then
                echo "${specific_product_version//[$'\t\r\n']}"
                return 0
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    # Getting the version number with productVersion.txt has failed. Try parsing the download link for a version number.
    say_verbose "Failed to get the version using productVersion.txt file. Download link will be parsed instead."
    specific_product_version="$(get_product_specific_version_from_download_link "$package_download_link" "$specific_version")"
    echo "${specific_product_version//[$'\t\r\n']}"
    return 0
}

patches.old:
get_remote_file_size() {
    local zip_uri="$1"

    if machine_has "curl"; then
        file_size=$(curl -sI  "$zip_uri" | grep -i content-length | awk '{ num = $2 + 0; print num }')
    elif machine_has "wget"; then
        file_size=$(wget --spider --server-response -O /dev/null "$zip_uri" 2>&1 | grep -i 'Content-Length:' | awk '{ num = $2 + 0; print num }')
    else
        say "Neither curl nor wget is available on this system."
        return
    fi

    if [ -n "$file_size" ]; then
        say "Remote file $zip_uri size is $file_size bytes."
        echo "$file_size"
    else
        say_verbose "Content-Length header was not extracted for $zip_uri."
        echo ""
    fi
}

set -eu
export DOTNET_ROOT="$OFFLINE_PREFIX"
export DOTNET_CLI_HOME="$HOME/.dotnet-cli"
export NUGET_PACKAGES="$HOME/.nuget/packages"
export DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1
export DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE=1
export DOTNET_NOLOGO=1
export DOTNET_GENERATE_ASPNET_CERTIFICATE=false
export DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH=false
export DOTNET_CLI_WORKLOAD_UPDATE_NOTIFY_DISABLE=true
project=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/csharp-project.XXXXXX")
"$OFFLINE_PREFIX/dotnet" new console --framework net10.0 --no-restore --output "$project"
cat > "$project/NuGet.Config" <<'CONFIG'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<configuration><packageSources><clear /></packageSources></configuration>
CONFIG
cat > "$project/Program.cs" <<'CS'
using System;
using System.Globalization;
using System.Linq;
using System.Text.Json;
var value = Enumerable.Range(1, 10).Sum();
var culture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("fr-FR");
var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(new { sum = value, decimalSeparator = culture.NumberFormat.NumberDecimalSeparator });
if (value != 55 || culture.NumberFormat.NumberDecimalSeparator != ",") throw new Exception("Functional assertion failed");
Console.WriteLine("SHELLFERRY_DOTNET_OK " + json);
CS
"$OFFLINE_PREFIX/dotnet" restore "$project" --configfile "$project/NuGet.Config" --packages "$NUGET_PACKAGES" -p:NuGetAudit=false
"$OFFLINE_PREFIX/dotnet" build "$project" --no-restore -c Release -p:NuGetAudit=false -p:UseSharedCompilation=false --nologo
"$OFFLINE_PREFIX/dotnet" run --project "$project" --no-build --no-restore -c Release > "$project/result.txt"
grep -q 'SHELLFERRY_DOTNET_OK' "$project/result.txt"
grep -q '"sum":55' "$project/result.txt"
grep -q '"decimalSeparator":","' "$project/result.txt"
cat "$project/result.txt"
"$OFFLINE_PREFIX/dotnet" --list-sdks | grep -q '^10.0.403 '
"$OFFLINE_PREFIX/dotnet" --list-runtimes | grep -q '^Microsoft.NETCore.App 10.0.14 '
notes: Converts Microsoft dotnet-install.sh at a fixed commit; current official dot.net/v1 entrypoint had identical bytes. Pins active LTS .NET 10 SDK 10.0.403 with runtime 10.0.14.

Preserves official argument parsing, OS/architecture/product-version selection, archive extraction, version-directory install behavior, size comparison, and already-installed handling. Only downloader prerequisite, network transport, product-version fetch transport, and HTTP size lookup are adapted.

SDK archive matches Microsoft official release-metadata SHA-512; the offline download adapter verifies that SHA-512 again before the original installer extracts it. Every source and resource also has a SHA-256 pin.

Includes the complete SDK, C# compiler, .NET/ASP.NET runtimes, reference packs and templates from the official SDK archive. Does not include optional workloads, cross-target runtime packs or external NuGet packages.

Ubuntu 22.04 runtime library prerequisites: libc6, libgcc-s1, libgssapi-krb5-2, libicu70, libssl3, libstdc++6, zlib1g (plus ca-certificates for future HTTPS use). These are explicitly prepared in the recorded test image and are not bundled system-library installers.

The offline C# test creates a fresh console project, clears all NuGet feeds, restores only SDK-provided framework references, builds and runs it, and asserts LINQ, JSON serialization and real French ICU culture data. Telemetry, workload update notifications and development-certificate generation are disabled.
Installs directly under the requested prefix. Run <prefix>/dotnet or add that prefix to PATH; the official --no-path option is preserved. No host installation or shell profile editing is performed.
